result.topic_en: Gauss gives algebraic substitutions for sin φ in terms of sin ψ that transform elliptic differentials, yielding transformations of the elliptic integral of the first kind of degree 3 and degree 5 (multiplication of the integral by 3 and by 5).
result.transcription:
Math. 25 \quad (91) [-47d/40-]
A. Setzt man
$\sin\varphi = \frac{\sin\psi\,(ac + (\frac{a-c}{2})^2 \sin\psi^2)}{cc + (\frac{a-c}{2})(\frac{a+3c}{2})\sin\psi^2}$
so wird
$\frac{d\varphi}{\sqrt{(a^3c - (\frac{a-c}{2})(\frac{a+3c}{2})^3 \sin\varphi^2)}} = \frac{d\psi}{\sqrt{(c^3a - (\frac{a-c}{2})^3\, \frac{a+3c}{2}) \sin\psi^2)}}$
B. Setzt man ferner
$\sin\psi = \frac{\sin\theta\,(-3ac + (\frac{a+3c}{2})^2 \sin\theta^2)}{aa - 3(\frac{a-c}{2})(\frac{a+3c}{2})\sin\theta^2}$
und
$\frac{a-c}{2c}\left(\frac{a+3c}{2a}\right)^3 = k$
so wird $\frac{d\varphi}{\sqrt{(1-k\sin\varphi^2)}} = \frac{3\,d\theta}{\sqrt{(1-k\sin\theta^2)}}$

A. Es sei $a^3 = 2b(1+a+b)$
und $\sin\varphi = \frac{\sin\psi\,(1+2a+(aa+2ab+2b)\sin\psi^2 + bb\sin\psi^4)}{1+(aa+2a+2b)\sin\psi^2 + b(b+2a)\sin\psi^4}$
so wird
$\int\frac{d\varphi}{\sqrt{((a-2b)(1+2a)^2 - (2-a)(b+2a)^2\sin\varphi^2)}} = \frac{d\psi}{\sqrt{(a-2b - bb(2-a)\sin\psi^2)}}$
B. Es sei $\alpha = \frac{2-a}{1+2a}$, $\mathfrak{b} = -\left(\frac{b+2a}{1+2a}\right)\left(\frac{2-a}{a-2b}\right)$, $\frac{2-a}{a-2b}\left(\frac{b+2a}{1+2a}\right)^2 = k$
ferner setze man
$\sin\psi = \frac{\sin\theta\,(1+2\alpha+(\alpha\alpha+2\alpha\mathfrak{b}+2\mathfrak{b})\sin\theta^2 + \mathfrak{b}\mathfrak{b}\sin\theta^4)}{1+(\alpha\alpha+2\alpha+2\mathfrak{b})\sin\theta^2 + \mathfrak{b}(\mathfrak{b}+2\alpha)\sin\theta^4}$
so wird
$\int\frac{d\varphi}{\sqrt{(1-k\sin\varphi^2)}} = 5\int\frac{d\theta}{\sqrt{(1-k\sin\theta^2)}}$

methods.what: Cubic (degree-3) transformation of the elliptic differential via a rational substitution for sin φ in terms of sin ψ
Resulting equality of differentials under the cubic transformation
Composition with a second (complementary) cubic transformation gives multiplication by 3 of the elliptic integral of the first kind with modulus parameter k
Definition of the parameter k for the triplication
Quintic (degree-5) transformation with the modular relation a^3 = 2b(1+a+b) and a rational substitution of degree 5
Resulting equality of differentials under the quintic transformation
Composition with a second quintic transformation (parameters α, 𝔟) gives multiplication by 5 of the elliptic integral of the first kind
